item.title: Tech giant Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets but acquitted of racketeering
item.description: In a statement, Huawei said the acquittal on the racketeering charge "confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years."

item.title: Europe Tonight debriefs: can the EU budget compete with China and the US?
item.description: Euronews' daily evening show Europe Tonight welcomed Lukas Gutenberg, director of Bertelsmann Stiftung, to discuss issues such as how the EU plans to do more with less, as well as the latest proposal put forward by Antonio Costa, which foresees another round of big cuts.

item.title: 'It's simply cheaper to fund Ukraine': Ukrainian economist warns Europe against cutting aid to Kyiv
item.description: Cutting financial support for Kyiv risks emboldening Moscow and exposing Europe to further Russian aggression, Tymofiy Mylovanov told Euronews. He warned that forcing Ukraine into concessions without credible security guarantees could pave the way for another war.

item.title: Europe Tonight: Europe faces tough budget negotiations
item.description: To debrief on the EU's passing of its budget, our correspondent Maria Tadeo spoke to Slovak MEP for Progressive Slovakia within the Renew Europe group Lucia Yar on Euronews' new weekly evening show Europe Tonight.

item.title: Miro G cargo vessel refloated after running aground off southwest France
item.description: France's Atlantic Maritime Prefecture said that "no marine pollution was detected in the area where the ship ran aground or along its transit route."

item.title: EU won't return to Russian energy regardless of US-led peace talks, Jørgensen tells Euronews
item.description: EU Energy chief tells Euronews Brussels will press ahead with its Russian gas ban regardless of the outcome of US-Russia peace talks.

item.title: At least 24 injured after car bomb detonates in central Colombia
item.description: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella arrived in Villavicencio at around 9 am local time on Tuesday as he prepared to hold a security meeting and visit the scene of the blast.

item.title: Matryoshka: What is the Russian disinformation campaign targeting Spain's election?
item.description: Spain is heading to the polls this weekend, in an election marred by disinformation online. With France, Italy and Poland also holding elections in the coming months, how prepared is Europe to deal with a new wave of fake political news?

item.title: Indonesia names former police chief as treason suspect in presidential wiretapping case
item.description: An investigation into alleged surveillance of Indonesia’s president has widened into a treason case against senior police figures. It has already led to dismissals and parliamentary scrutiny, with police alleging a plot to undermine Prabowo’s government.

item.title: Pope Francis' private notes reveal visions of the devil and a plan to allow married men to be priests
item.description: The book published on Tuesday contains Jorge Mario Bergoglio's notes over 30 years, including meetings with the devil, a spiritual crisis, and his choice on married priests.

item.title: Europe Tonight: EU budget battle, €45B Ukraine aid, and Serbia-Kosovo tensions
item.description: Europe Tonight unpacks the fierce clash in Brussels over the EU’s next seven-year budget and a proposed €45 billion loan package for Ukraine, examines Serbia-Kosovo diplomatic tensions ahead of the Western Balkans summit with former Kosovo President Vjosa Osmani, and features an exclusive interview

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 24th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 24th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: UK warns defence suppliers to Ukraine over Russian sabotage
item.description: The warning follows a fresh wave of security incidents across Europe in recent weeks, including airspace violations and reported cyber and sabotage attacks.

item.title: New terms and conditions: Tidal bans AI music in a bid to promote fairness in industry
item.description: The streaming giant says its begun moves to ban and remove up to 29 million AI generated tracks from its platform in a decision it predicts will be welcomed by artists and fans alike.

item.title: MEPs call on the Commission to assess human rights in Rwanda amid return hub plans
item.description: The letter signed by 76 MEPs targets a controversial plan to set up a centre in Rwanda for migrants with no legal right to stay in Europe.

item.title: Italy watches worryingly as Ukraine strikes Russian boats in Libya
item.description: Ukraine's naval drone strikes on two Russian vessels in and off Benghazi have alarmed Italy, amid fears that the attacks could reignite Libya's civil war.

item.title: Colombia: At least 25 injured in bombing as armed violence resurges
item.description: At least 25 people were injured in a bombing in Villavicencio, damaging government buildings, businesses and vehicles. Meanwhile, hundreds of residents marched with candles in Cúcuta following a separate attack, amid a resurgence of armed violence in Colombia.

item.title: Italy develops 'ambitious' business with 'strategic partner' Azerbaijan, Tajani tells Euronews
item.description: Italy's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Euronews that Rome has sought to expand its business relations with Baku now that peace has brought stability and improved connectivity to the region.

item.title: Two arrested on suspicion of burglary at Prince and Princess of Wales' UK country home
item.description: Two men were arrested on the Sandringham estate on suspicion of burglary and trespass and remain in custody, Norfolk Police said. The force added that the property was unoccupied at the time of the incident.

item.title: Why French pharma firm Sanofi is paying $41 billion for US company Insmed
item.description: French drugmaker Sanofi has agreed a $41 billion (€37.4bn) all-cash takeover of Insmed, a US biopharma company. The deal, one of its biggest ever, is meant to refill its pipeline of new medicines before its best-selling drug loses patent protection.

item.title: ‘Pervert glasses’ named Word of the Year by Macquarie dictionary
item.description: The Australian dictionary’s committee of word experts said the winning term is "a succinct reflection of the state of the world in 2026". 'Pervert glasses' follows ‘enshittification’ in 2024 and ‘AI slop’ in 2025.

item.title: Visegrad leaders demand delay to ETS2, piling pressure on EU's carbon market
item.description: Poland, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic want to soften the bloc's expanded carbon market ahead of the 26-27 November European Council

item.title: Migrant caravans head north through Mexico towards US border
item.description: Migrants from several Central American countries are travelling through southern Mexico in a caravan, hoping to reach the United States.

item.title: Senegal reinstated as AFCON champions as Morocco vows to fight on
item.description: The sport's top court ruled that the referee's decision to restart the final after Senegal's walk-off could not be challenged, while Morocco has raised questions over alleged contact between one of the judges and Senegal's federation.

item.title: South Korea tells island residents to take shelter as Russian warplanes near its airspace
item.description: South Korea has repeatedly scrambled fighter jets in response to Russian military flights. Tuesday’s approach to an inhabited island brought a rare shelter warning for civilians, although the aircraft stayed outside the country’s territorial airspace.

item.title: Slovakia moves to scrap postal voting for citizens living abroad
item.description: The proposed changes have prompted protests across the country. The opposition has said the measure targets pro-Western voters and that it could stop tens of thousands of Slovaks from voting.

item.title: Qatar says it ‘will not accept’ attacks after Iran protests over joint statement with Germany
item.description: Iran summoned a Qatari diplomat in Tehran over a joint statement with Germany condemning Iranian attacks and threats to shipping. Qatar said it will handle the dispute through diplomacy and that both the US and Iran were still participating in its mediation efforts.

item.title: How Trump and Silicon Valley got Nvidia to bring back Jensen Huang
item.description: Nvidia's board said Jensen Huang would not return. Six days later, the chipmaker announced his reinstatement after Donald Trump pressed for his return and Elon Musk backed the campaign. Here's how the reversal unfolded and what was at stake for the AI industry.

item.title: At least 490,000 Russian soldiers killed in Ukraine, Rosstat data leak reveals
item.description: Two hacking groups extracted the data from the statistics agency's systems on 1 November. The figure comes from death certificates registered up to the end of August, so it excludes missing servicemen and deaths not yet recorded.

item.title: Scientists discover quasar formed 630 million years after the Big Bang
item.description: The discovery makes the quasar, extremely bright galactic cores powered by giant black holes, the most distant one ever recorded.

item.title: French police officer who killed teenager Nahel to stand trial for murder
item.description: Judges reversed an earlier downgrade of the charge, ruling that a shot to the chest fired from 16cm pointed to an intent to kill. The officer now faces up to 30 years in prison.

item.title: France: Chefs compete for the world egg mayonnaise championship
item.description: Sixteen finalists gathered near Paris to compete for the title of world egg mayonnaise champion, held in Saint-Ouen, just outside Paris, on Monday 23 November 2026. The competition celebrates a deceptively simple French bistro classic that demands considerable culinary skill.

item.title: European court rules against Poland and Latvia over migrant pushbacks at Belarus border
item.description: The judgment from the European Court of Human Rights concerns separate incidents from 2021, when Belarus facilitated the movement of irregular migrants towards EU borders as a means of exerting political pressure, prompting Polish and Latvian authorities to intercept and immediately return them.

item.title: Hungary’s rule-of-law reforms: ‘We’re not done yet,’ warns Green MEP Daniel Freund
item.description: German Green MEP Daniel Freund has warned against ending the EU's rule-of-law proceedure against Hungary too soon.

item.title: ‘A disaster’: Frederiksen's migration stance sparks tensions within European Socialists
item.description: Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen drew sharp criticism after making controversial remarks on migration in a domestic podcast, emphasising Denmark's "ethnically Danish" population and appearing to echo the far-right "great replacement" theory.

item.title: Too little soil, too little water: how two countries are reinventing farming
item.description: In the Maldives, farmers grow crops on nutrient-poor coral sand. Thousands of kilometres away, Uzbekistan monitors farmland from space. Despite their different environments, both countries are finding ways to tackle a major challenge: producing food with limited resources.

item.title: Growing health inequalities put millions of European children at risk, WHO warns
item.description: The report highlights how health inequalities affect children from disadvantaged backgrounds, shaping their development and opportunities from the earliest stages of life.

item.title: Was it a lion? Grainy footage prompted a large search in Istanbul
item.description: Reports of a lioness roaming north of Istanbul prompted a security scramble after grainy footage appeared to show a large cat prowling across open land. Following a day of searches, Turkish authorities said the animal was neither a lion nor any other big cat.

item.title: Red lines, political horse-trading and Ukraine: Inside the EU's increasingly bitter budget battle
item.description: EU capitals are divided on several fronts ahead of key talks on the bloc's next long-term budget: overall size, political priorities, Ukraine financing and new EU taxes. Tense domestic politics make compromise harder, with only leaders expected to break the deadlock.

item.title: China and Singapore expand yuan financing as Beijing pushes currency’s global use
item.description: China is encouraging more trade and investment in yuan, although the currency remains far less widely used than the dollar. Singapore’s new financing plans would give businesses more ways to access yuan, including funding for trade with other countries.

item.title: Doctors warn of pesticide risk to fertility as EU moves to cut red tape
item.description: Pesticide exposure may affect people’s fertility, but more conclusive research is needed.

item.title: Germany sees rising violence against women as minister plans femicide law reform
item.description: The number of victims of domestic violence was higher in 2025 than ever before, according to new reports from the Federal Criminal Police Office. Violence against women and girls has risen across many categories of offences.

item.title: US and Armenia launch Trump-backed regional transit route as Baku welcomes move
item.description: A year after the Washington summit that brought peace between Armenia and Azerbaijan, the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) project has entered its construction phase amid broader geopolitical reshaping in the region and beyond.

item.title: Israeli strikes kill Hamas security chief and six others in Gaza
item.description: Two policemen died when a police station in southern Gaza was hit, while coalition talks in Israel leave caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu in charge of military operations.

item.title: Pet passports to return from 2028 for Brits travelling to the EU with cats, dogs and ferrets
item.description: The rule change will mean pet owners no longer need to fork out for an animal health certificate each time they travel.

item.title: France to create strategic reserves of rare earths and critical metals
item.description: This project was announced on Monday by Emmanuel Macron during a closed-door meeting with industrialists at the Élysée. These mineral stocks will be accompanied by a mechanism of "joint purchases".

item.title: International Space Forum in Rome gathers 45 countries to shape future space rules
item.description: The new orbital economy is worth billions and increasingly involves private operators. Europe is seeking a strategy to avoid losing ground.

item.title: West's weak response to Litvinenko's murder emboldened Putin, widow tells Euronews
item.description: Twenty years after her husband's murder in London, one of the most notorious Russian intelligence operations on foreign soil, Marina Litvinenko warns Europe against negotiating with Putin from a position of weakness and says justice requires a trial of his regime in Russia.

item.title: How Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia made the world trillions richer
item.description: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO made him about $34 billion (€31bn) richer and added roughly $950 billion (€871bn) to the chipmaker's value in a single day. US President Donald Trump, Nvidia's staff and stock markets from New York to Seoul gained too, while Europe got a smaller lift.

item.title: Carbon capture was a sticking point at COP31: Is it a delay tactic or genuine solution?
item.description: The technology has been found to be “technically uncertain and very high cost” - yet the European Commission is funding it.
